name: Seared rockfish, brown butter, and the October salad
intro: A fish most people walk past, seared hard and finished in brown butter, over roasted kabocha, with a salad of arugula, pomegranate, dates, and feta that only works this month.

steps.text: Heat the oven. Toss the kabocha with oil and salt and roast until the edges are dark and a knife slides through.
Salt the fish and leave it on a plate, then pat it completely dry.
Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high with a thin film of oil until it shimmers. Lay the fillets in, away from you.
Don't touch them. They're ready to flip when the edges turn opaque and the fish lets go of the pan on its own.
Flip, add the butter, and tilt the pan, spooning the foaming butter over the fish until it smells nutty and turns golden brown. Squeeze in half the lemon.
Put the arugula, pomegranate, dates, and feta in a bowl. Dress it at the table with olive oil, the rest of the lemon, and salt.
Fish over the kabocha, brown butter spooned on top, the salad beside it, ajvar on the table.

how_it_works: The sear is October's lesson: dry fish, a hot pan, and hands off until it lets go on its own — that's how a crust forms instead of sticking. Brown butter is the reward: butter cooked until its milk solids toast, which gives a mild fish everything it lacks.
swaps: Any firm white fillet — cod or halibut — works the same way.
Skip the brown butter; finish with warm chile-garlic oil and lime instead.
